34.subject: Botany
34.text: Select the option that correctly matches characteristic features with the group of three animals.
options: Skeleton of spicules - Sycon, Adamsia, Spongilla
Excretion by flame - Taenia, Fasciola, cells Ancylostoma
34.sol: In poriferans, the body is supported by a skeleton made up of spicules or spongin fibres. Sycon and Spongilla are examples of poriferans, whereas Adamsia is a coelenterate. In platyhelminths, specialised cells called flame cells help in excretion. Taenia and Fasciola are platyhelminths whereas Ancylostoma is an aschelminth. In molluscs, mouth contains a file-like rasping organ for feeding called radula. Dentalium and Octopus are molluscs whereas Ophiura is an echinoderm. Arthropods have jointed appendages. Limulus, Apis and Laccifer all three are arthropods.
34.meta: Select the option that correctly matches characteristic features with the group of three animals.

1256.subject: Physics
1256.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
1256.text: A ball is bouncing down a flight of stairs. The coefficient of restitution is $e$. The height of each step is $d$ and the ball descends one step each bounce. After each bounce it rebounds to a height $h$ above the next lower step. The height is large enough compared with the width of step so that the impacts are effectively head-on. Find the relationship between $h$ and $d$.
1256.sol:
The ball falls a distance $h$ from its highest (rest) position and rebounds a distance $(h-d)$.
Thus the coefficient of restitution $e=\sqrt{\frac{h-d}{h}}$ $e^2=\frac{h-d}{h} \quad$ or $\quad h=\frac{d}{1-e^2}$

7441.sol:
$a=\cos \left(\frac{8 \pi}{11}\right)+i \sin \left(\frac{8 \pi}{11}\right) \Rightarrow a=e^{\frac{i 8 \pi}{11}}$
$\Rightarrow a$ is 11 th root of unity and all roots are $1, a, a^2, \ldots, a^{10}$
Now, $\quad a^{10}=\frac{a^{10} \cdot a}{a}=\frac{a^{11}}{a}=\frac{1}{a}=\bar{a}$
Similarly, $a^9=\overline{a^2}, a^8=\overline{a^3}, a^7=\overline{a^4}, a^6=\overline{a^5}$,
We know that,
Sum of $n$ roots of unity $=0$
$$
\begin{gathered}
1+a^1+a^2+a^3+\ldots+a^{10}=0 \\
\Rightarrow a+a^2+a^3+a^4+a^5+a^6+a^7+a^8 \\
a^9+a^{10}=-1 \\
\Rightarrow(a+\bar{a})+\left(a^2+\overline{a^2}\right)+\left(a^3+\overline{a^3}\right) \\
+\left(a^4+\overline{a^4}\right)+\left(a^5+\overline{a^5}\right)=-1 \\
\Rightarrow 2 \operatorname{Re}(a)+2 \operatorname{Re}\left(a^2\right)+2 \operatorname{Re}\left(a^3\right)+2 \operatorname{Re}\left(a^4\right)+2 \operatorname{Re}\left(a^5\right) \\
=-1[z+\bar{z}=2 \operatorname{Re}(z)] \\
\Rightarrow 2 \operatorname{Re}\left(a+a^2+a^3+a^4+a^5\right)=-1 \\
\Rightarrow \operatorname{Re}\left(a+a^2+a^3+a^4+a^5\right)=-\frac{1}{2}
\end{gathered}
$$

8095.text: If $\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} y(x)=\frac{\pi}{2}$, then the solution of $x^3 \sin y \frac{d y}{d x}=2$ is $\cos y=$

$\because \quad x^3 \sin y \frac{d y}{d x}=2 \Rightarrow \sin y d y=\frac{2}{x^3} d x$
Integrating both sides, we get
$\int \sin y d y=2 \int \frac{1}{x^3} d x \Rightarrow-\cos y=2 \cdot \frac{x^{-2}}{-2}+C\Rightarrow \quad \cos y=\frac{1}{x^2}-C$ ...(i)
Taking $\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}$ on both sides :
$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad \lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \cos y=\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{x^2}-C \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \cos \left(\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} y\right)=0-C \Rightarrow \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=-C \Rightarrow C=0\end{aligned}$
Putting the value of $C$ in equation (i), we get :
$\Rightarrow \quad \cos y=\frac{1}{x^2}-0 \Rightarrow \cos y=\frac{1}{x^2}$

$I=\int e^{4 x^2+8 x-4}(x+1) \cos \left(3 x^2+6 x-4\right) d x$
Let $x^2+2 x=t \Rightarrow(x+1) d x=\frac{d t}{2}I=\frac{1}{2} \int e^{4 t-4} \cos (3 t-4) d t$
We know, $\int e^{a x} \cos (b x+c) d x=\frac{e^{a x}}{a^2+b^2}(a \cos (b x+c)+b \sin (b x+c))\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow I=\frac{1}{2} \frac{e^{4 t-4}}{16+9}(4 \cos (3 t-4)+3 \sin (3 t-4))+c \\ & \Rightarrow I=\frac{e^{4 x^2+8 x-2}}{50}\left[4 \cos \left(3 x^2+6 x-4\right)+3 \sin \left(3 x^2+6 x-4\right)\right]+c\end{aligned}$

\(\begin{aligned}
& I=\int\left(\frac{x^3-1}{x^3+x}\right) d x=\int\left(1-\frac{x+1}{x^3+x}\right) d x \\
& \Rightarrow \int 1 \cdot d x-\int \frac{(x+1)}{x^3+x} d x=x-\int \frac{(x+1)}{x\left(x^2+1\right)} d x
\end{aligned}\)
Now, \(\frac{x+1}{x\left(x^2+1\right)}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B x+C}{x^2+1}\)
\(\Rightarrow \quad(x+1)=A\left(x^2+1\right)+(B x+C) x\)
[using partial fractions]
\(\Rightarrow \quad(x+1)=(A+B) x^2+C x+A\)
On comparing \(A+B=0, C=1, A=1\)
\(\begin{array}{lc}
\Rightarrow & B=-1 \\
\therefore & I=x-\int \frac{1}{x} d x-\int \frac{(1-x)}{x^2+1} d x \\
\Rightarrow & I=x-\log |x|-\int \frac{1}{x^2+1} d x+\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{2 x}{x^2+1} d x \\
\Rightarrow & I=x-\log |x|-\tan ^{-1} x+\frac{1}{2} \log \left(x^2+1\right)+C

9426.text: If $\int x^3 e^{5 x} d x=\frac{e^{5 x}}{5^4}[f(x)]+C$, then $f(x)$ is equal to
9426.sol:
We have given that,
$\int x^3 e^{5 x} d x=\frac{e^{5 x}}{5^4}\left[\int(x)\right]+c$
By using the method of intergration by parts, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& \int x^3 e^{5 x} d x=x^3 \int e^{5 x} d x-\int\left\{\frac{d x^3}{d x} \int e^{5 x} d x\right\} d x \\
& =\frac{x^3 e^{5 x}}{5}-\int \frac{3 x^2 e^{5 x}}{5} d x+C
\end{aligned}$
By using the method of integration by parts, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& =\frac{x^3 e^{5 x}}{5}-\frac{3}{5} x^2 \int e^{5 x} d x \\
& +\frac{3}{5} \int\left\{\frac{d x^2}{d x} \int e^{5 x} d x\right\} d x+C \\
& =\frac{x^3 e^{5 x}}{5}-\frac{3 x^3 e^{5 x}}{25}+\frac{6}{25} \int x e^{5 x} d x \\
& =\frac{x^3 e^{5 x}}{5}-\frac{3 x^3 e^{5 x}}{25}+\frac{6 x}{25} \int e^{5 x} d x \\
& -\frac{6}{25} \int\left\{\frac{d x}{d x} \int e^{5 x} d x\right\} d x \\
& =\frac{x^3 e^{5 x}}{5}-\frac{3 x^3 e^{5 x}}{25}+\frac{6 x e^{5 x}}{125}-\frac{6}{125} \int e^{5 x} d x
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& =\frac{x^3 e^{5 x}}{5}-\frac{3 x^3 e^{5 x}}{25}+\frac{6 x e^{5 x}}{125}-\frac{6}{125}+C \\
& =\frac{e^{5 x}}{625}\left[125 x^3-75 x^2+30 x-6\right]+C
\end{aligned}$
Comparing the above equation with
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{e^{5 x}}{5^4}[f(x)]+C, \text{ we get } \\
& f(x)=5^3 x^3-75 x^2+30 x-6
\end{aligned}$

19500.text:
Two statements, Assertion and Reason are given below. Choose the correct option.
Assertion: n-propyl tert-butyl ether can be readily prepared in the laboratory by Williamson's synthesis.
Reason: The reaction occurs by $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}} 1$ attack of Primary alkoxide on Tert-alkyl halide to give good yield of the product, n-propyl tert-butyl ether.
options: Assertion is incorrect but reason is correct.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
19500.sol:
Assertion is correct: n-propyl tert-butyl ether can be prepared by Williamson synthesis by reacting sodium tert-butoxide (tertiary alkoxide) with 1-bromopropane (primary alkyl halide) via $S_N2$.

Reason is incorrect for two reasons: Williamson synthesis proceeds via $S_N2$, not $S_N1$. Also, if a primary alkoxide attacks a tert-alkyl halide, the strong base would cause E2 elimination (forming isobutylene) rather than substitution, giving very poor yield of the ether.

Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.

20121.sol:
A reducing agent undergoes oxidation. The strength of a reducing agent is directly proportional to its standard oxidation potential, which is the negative of its standard reduction potential.

The standard oxidation potentials for the given species are:
$E^o_{\text{Cr}/\text{Cr}^{3+}} = -(-0.74) = +0.74$ V
$E^o_{\text{Cl}^-/\text{Cl}_2} = -1.36$ V
$E^o_{\text{Mn}^{2+}/\text{MnO}_4^-} = -1.51$ V
$E^o_{\text{Cr}^{3+}/\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}} = -1.33$ V

Since $Cr$ has the highest standard oxidation potential ($+0.74$ V), it has the greatest tendency to get oxidized. Therefore, $Cr$ is the strongest reducing agent among the given options.

Answer: $Cr$

21345.text: The particular solution of $\dfrac{d y}{d x}+\sqrt{\dfrac{1-y^2}{1-x^2}}=0$, when $x=0, y=\dfrac{1}{2}$ is
21345.sol:
The given differential equation is $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \sqrt{\dfrac{1-y^2}{1-x^2}} = 0$.

Separating the variables, we have $\dfrac{dy}{\sqrt{1-y^2}} = -\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$.

Integrating both sides, we get $\int \dfrac{dy}{\sqrt{1-y^2}} = -\int \dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$.

This yields $\sin^{-1} y = -\sin^{-1} x + C$, which simplifies to $\sin^{-1} x + \sin^{-1} y = C$.

Given the initial condition $x=0$ and $y=\dfrac{1}{2}$, we substitute these values into the equation:

$\sin^{-1}(0) + \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = C$.

$0 + \dfrac{\pi}{6} = C$, so $C = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

Therefore, the particular solution is $\sin^{-1} x + \sin^{-1} y = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

Answer: $\sin ^{-1} x+\sin ^{-1} y=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$

21848.subject: Mathematics
21848.text: How many factors of $2^5 \times 3^6 \times 5^2$ are perfect squares?
21848.sol:
The given number is $N = 2^{5} \times 3^{6} \times 5^{2}$.

A factor of $N$ is of the form $2^{a} \times 3^{b} \times 5^{c}$, where $0 \le a \le 5$, $0 \le b \le 6$, and $0 \le c \le 2$.

For the factor to be a perfect square, the exponents $a, b, c$ must be even integers.

The possible values for $a$ are $0, 2, 4$ (3 values).

The possible values for $b$ are $0, 2, 4, 6$ (4 values).

The possible values for $c$ are $0, 2$ (2 values).

The total number of such factors is the product of the number of choices for each exponent:

$3 \times 4 \times 2 = 24$.

Answer: 24

The Venn diagram shows two sets $A$ and $B$ within a universal set $U$.

The region $A \cup B$ represents the union of sets $A$ and $B$, which includes all elements that are in $A$, in $B$, or in both.

The shaded region in the diagram is the area outside both circles $A$ and $B$. This represents the complement of the union of $A$ and $B$, denoted as $(A \cup B)^{\prime}$.

According to De Morgan's Law, $(A \cup B)^{\prime} = A^{\prime} \cap B^{\prime}$.

Therefore, the shaded region represents $A^{\prime} \cap B^{\prime}$.

Answer: $A^{\prime} \cap B^{\prime}$

23243.subject: Physics
23243.text: A hockey player hits the ball at an angle of $37^{{}^{\circ}}$ from the horizontal with an initial speed of $40 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$ (a right angled triangle with one of the angle is $37^{{}^{\circ}}$ and their sides in the ratio of $6: 8: 10$). Assume that the ball is in a vertical plane. The time at which the ball reaches the highest point of its path is
23243.sol:
The initial velocity of the ball is $u = 40 \text{ m/s}$ and the angle of projection is $\theta = 37^{{}^{\circ}}$.

The vertical component of the initial velocity is given by $u_y = u \sin \theta$.

Given the triangle with sides in ratio $3:4:5$ (which is equivalent to $6:8:10$), $\sin 37^{{}^{\circ}} = \dfrac{3}{5}$.

Substituting the values, $u_y = 40 \times \dfrac{3}{5} = 8 \times 3 = 24 \text{ m/s}$.

At the highest point of the trajectory, the vertical component of the velocity becomes zero, $v_y = 0$.

Using the equation of motion $v_y = u_y - gt$, where $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$ is the acceleration due to gravity:

$0 = 24 - 10t$

$10t = 24$

$t = 2.4 \text{ s}$.

Answer: 2.4 s

23635.subject: Physics
23635.text: In a Young's double slit experiment, the slits are separated by 0.5 mm. Fringes are obtained on a screen which is placed at distance 1 m away from the slits. When the screen is moved 7 cm farther away, the fringe width changes by 63 $\mu$ m. The wavelength of light used in the experiment will be:
23635.sol:
The fringe width in a Young's double slit experiment is given by $\beta = \dfrac{\lambda D}{d}$

When the screen is moved by a distance $\Delta D$, the change in fringe width is $\Delta \beta = \dfrac{\lambda \Delta D}{d}$

Rearranging the formula to solve for the wavelength $\lambda$:

$\lambda = \dfrac{\Delta \beta \cdot d}{\Delta D}$

Substituting the given values $\Delta \beta = 63 \times 10^{-6}\ m$, $d = 0.5 \times 10^{-3}\ m$, and $\Delta D = 7 \times 10^{-2}\ m$:

$\lambda = \dfrac{63 \times 10^{-6} \times 0.5 \times 10^{-3}}{7 \times 10^{-2}}$

$\lambda = \dfrac{31.5 \times 10^{-9}}{7 \times 10^{-2}}$

$\lambda = 4.5 \times 10^{-7}\ m$

Answer: $4.5 \times 10^{-7}\ m$

26348.text: A long circular tube of length $10 \mathrm{~m}$ and radius $0.3 \mathrm{~m}$ carries a current I along its curved surface as shown. A wire loop of resistance $0.005 \Omega$ and of radius $0.1 \mathrm{~m}$ is placed inside the tube with its axis coinciding with the axis of the tube. The current varies as $I=I_0 \cos 300 t$, where $I_0$ is constant. If the magnetic moment of the loop is $N \mu_0 I_0 \sin 300 t$, then $N$ is
26348.sol:
Take the circular tube as a long solenoid. The wires are closely wound. Magnetic field inside the solenoid is

B=\mu_0 n i

Here, $n=$ number of turns per unit length
$\therefore n i=$ current per unit length
In the given problem,

$\begin{aligned}$& n i=$\frac{I}{L}$\\
\therefore \quad B & =$\frac{\mu_0 I}{L}
\end{aligned}Flux passing through the $circular coil is

\phi=B S=$\left(\frac{\mu_0 I}{L}\right)\left(\pi$r^2\right)

Induced emf, $e=-\frac{d \phi}{d t}=-\left(\frac{\mu_0 \pi r^2}{L R}\right) \cdot \frac{d I}{d t}$
Induced current,

i=$\frac{e}{R}=-\left(\frac{\mu_0 \pi r^2}{L R}\right) \frac{d I}{d t}$Magnetic moment $i A=i \pi r^2$ or $\quad M=-\left(\frac{\mu_0 \pi^2 r^4}{L R}\right) \cdot \frac{d I}{d t}$
Given, $\quad I=I_0 \cos 300 t$
\therefore \quad $\frac{d I}{d t}=-$300 I_0 \sin (300 t)

Substituting$ in Eq. (i), we get\begin{aligned}$M & =$\left(\frac{300 \pi^2 r^4}{L R}\right) \mu_$0 I_0 \sin 300 t \\
\therefore \quad N & =$\frac{300 \pi^2 r^4}{L R}
\end{aligned}$Substituting the values, we get

$\begin{aligned}$N & =$\frac{300(22 / 7)^2(0.1)^4}{(10)(0.005)}$\\
& =5.926
\end{aligned}$ or \quad N \simeq 6$

26675.text:
Paragraph
A thermally insulating cylinder has a thermally insulating and frictionless movable partition in the middle, as shown in the figure below. On each side of the partition, there is one mole of an ideal gas, with specific heat at constant volume, $C_{V}=2 R$. Here, $R$ is the gas constant. Initially, each side has a volume $V_{0}$ and temperature $T_{0}$. The left side has an electric heater, which is turned on at very low power to transfer heat $Q$ to the gas on the left side. As a result the partition moves slowly towards the right reducing the right side volume to $V_{0} / 2$. Consequently, the gas temperatures on the left and the right sides become $T_{L}$ and $T_{R}$, respectively. Ignore the changes in the temperatures of the cylinder, heater and the partition.

QuestionThe value of $\dfrac{{T}_{R}}{{T}_{0}}$ is:
26675.sol:
Writing ${C}_{V}$ in terms of degree of freedom of the gas $f$, we get,

${C}_{V} = \dfrac{f}{2}R = 2R ⇒ f = 4,$

Therefore,​ adiabatic index of gas will be given by,​​​​​​$\gamma = 1 + \dfrac{2}{f} = 1 + \dfrac{2}{4} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

The gas of the right portion has undergone through an adiabatic process so,

${T}_{i}{V}_{i}^{\gamma - 1} = {T}_{f}{V}_{f}^{\gamma - 1} ⇒ {T}_{0}{V}_{0}^{\dfrac{3}{2} - 1} = {T}_{R}{\left(\dfrac{{V}_{0}}{2}\right)}^{\dfrac{3}{2} - 1}$

$⇒ {T}_{R} = \sqrt{2}{T}_{0} ⇒ \dfrac{{T}_{R}}{{T}_{0}} = \sqrt{2}$

31017.subject: Chemistry
31017.text: The difference between electron gain enthalpies will be maximum between :
31017.sol:
Electron gain enthalpy is defined as the amount of energy released when an electron is added to an isolated gaseous atom. During the addition of an electron, energy can either be released or absorbed. Electron gain enthalpy decreases down the group because as we move down the group, the size of an element increases, and the effective nuclear charge decreases. Due to this, the incoming electron will experience less attraction. Thus, electron gain enthalpy decreases as we move down the group.

${\Delta H}_{eg}$ for chlorine$= - 349kJ{mole}^{- 1}$

${\Delta H}_{eg}$ for Neon$= + 116kJ{mole}^{- 1}$

${\Delta H}_{eg}$ for Argon $= + 96{kJmol}^{- 1}$

${\Delta H}_{eg}$for fluorine $= - 333kJ{mol}^{- 1}$

33012.text: The distance from the origin, of the normal to the curve, $x = 2cos ⁡ t + 2tsin ⁡ t, y = 2sin ⁡ t - 2tcos ⁡ tatt = \dfrac{\pi}{4},$ is :
33012.sol:
At $t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$,

$x = 2\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + 2\dfrac{\pi}{4} . \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \left(\sqrt{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{2\sqrt{2}}\right) = \left(\dfrac{4 + \pi}{2\sqrt{2}}\right)$

$y = 2\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} - 2\dfrac{\pi}{4} ⋅ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \left(\sqrt{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{2\sqrt{2}}\right) = \left(\dfrac{4 - \pi}{2\sqrt{2}}\right)$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2cos ⁡ t - 2\left[cos ⁡ t + t ( - sin ⁡ t )\right] = 2tsin ⁡ t$

$\dfrac{dx}{dt} = - 2sin ⁡ t + 2\left[sin ⁡ t + t ⋅ cos ⁡ t\right] = 2tcos ⁡ t$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = tan ⁡ t$ at $t = \dfrac{\pi}{4} ⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = tan ⁡ \dfrac{\pi}{4} = 1$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1$ .

Slope of tangent is $1$ & therefore slope of normal would be $- 1$.

Equation of normal $y - \left(\dfrac{4 - \pi}{2\sqrt{2}}\right) = - 1\left(x - \left(\dfrac{4 + \pi}{2\sqrt{2}}\right)\right)$

$x + y = \left(\dfrac{4 + \pi}{2\sqrt{2}}\right) + \left(\dfrac{4 - \pi}{2\sqrt{2}}\right)$

$⇒ x + y = \dfrac{8}{2\sqrt{2}}$

Distance from origin $= \left|\dfrac{\dfrac{- 8}{2\sqrt{2}}}{\sqrt{2}}\right| = 2$

For any standard hyperbola we know that

eccentricity, $e = \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{{b}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}}$, conjugate axis $= 2b$ and distance between the foci $= 2ae$.

Given, $2b = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(2ae\right)$.

$⇒ {e}^{2} = \dfrac{4}{3}$

$⇒ e = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$

$∴ {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = \pm \sqrt{{a}^{2}{x}^{2} + {b}^{2}{y}^{2}}$

Squaring both sides,

36553.text: Two distinct numbers $a$ and $b$ are selected at random from $1,2,3, \ldots, 50$. The probability, that their product $a b$ is divisible by 3, is
36553.sol:
Total ways $= \binom{50}{2} = 1225$.
$ab$ is divisible by 3 iff at least one of $a, b$ is divisible by 3.
Multiples of 3 in $\{1,\ldots,50\}$: $3,6,\ldots,48 \Rightarrow 16$ numbers. Non-multiples of 3: $34$.
$P(\text{neither divisible by 3}) = \frac{\binom{34}{2}}{\binom{50}{2}} = \frac{561}{1225}$.
$P(ab \text{ divisible by 3}) = 1 - \frac{561}{1225} = \frac{664}{1225}$.

38982.text: An atom absorbs a photon of wavelength $500nm$ and emits another photon of wavelength $600nm$. The net energy absorbed by the atom in this process is $n \times {10}^{- 4}eV$. 38982.sol:
The energy of a photon is given by $E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$.

It is given that ${\lambda}_{1} = 500nm$, ${\lambda}_{2} = 600nm$.

The net energy absorbed is

$\DeltaE = \dfrac{hc}{{\lambda}_{1}} - \dfrac{hc}{{\lambda}_{2}} = \dfrac{hc}{{10}^{- 9}} ( \dfrac{1}{500} - \dfrac{1}{600} )$

$= \dfrac{6 . 6 \times {10}^{- 34} \times 3 \times {10}^{8} \times 100}{500 \times 600 \times {10}^{- 9}}$

$= \dfrac{6 . 6 \times 3}{30} \times {10}^{- 19}J$

$1eV = 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}J$

$= \dfrac{6 . 6 \times 3}{30 \times 1 . 6}eV$

$= 4125 \times {10}^{- 4}eV$

When the cells are connected in series ${i}_{s} = \dfrac{2ε}{2r + R} = \dfrac{2ε}{2r + 2}$

When they are connected in parallel, the emf is ${ε}_{p} = \dfrac{\dfrac{ε}{r} + \dfrac{ε}{r}}{\dfrac{1}{r} + \dfrac{1}{r}} = ε$ and the effective internal resistance will be ${r}_{p} = \dfrac{r \times r}{r + r} = \dfrac{r}{2}$. Therefore, the current will be,

${i}_{p} = \dfrac{ε}{R + \dfrac{r}{2}} = \dfrac{ε}{2 + \dfrac{r}{2}} = \dfrac{2ε}{4 + r}$

Since, ${i}_{s} = {i}_{p} ⇒ \dfrac{2ε}{2r + 2} = \dfrac{2ε}{4 + r} ⇒ r = 2Ω$
39673.meta: The combination of two identical cells, whether connected in series or parallel combination provides the same current through an external resistance of 2Ω .

\end{aligned} =5 \mathrm{eV}$

41871.text: Resistance of a given wire is obtained by measuring the current flowing in it and the voltage difference applied across it. If the percentage errors in the measurement of the current and the voltage difference are $3 \%$ each, then error in the value of resistance of the wire is

Similarly, $\frac{\Delta i}{i}=0.03$
Hence $\frac{\Delta \mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{R}}=0.06$
So percentage error is $\frac{\Delta \mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{R}} \times 100=6 \%$

42537.text: A radio active material is reduced to $\dfrac{1}{8}$ of its original amount in $3$ days. If $8 \times {10}^{- 3}kg$ of the material is left after $5$ days the initial amount of the material is
42537.sol:
The initial and final amount of the radioactive substance are related by the formula

$\dfrac{N}{{N}_{0}} = {\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{n} . . . \left(1\right)$

where, $n$ is the number of half lives.

Substitute $\dfrac{1}{8}$ for $\dfrac{N}{{N}_{0}}$ into equation (1) and solve to calculate the value of $n$.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{1}{8} & = & {\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{n} \\ & ⇒ & {\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{3} = {\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{n} \\ & ⇒ & n = 3\end{cases}$

The half-life of the radioactive element can be calculated as follows:

$\dfrac{t}{{t}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}} = n . . . \left(2\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (2) and solve to calculate the half-life.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{3days}{{t}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}} & = & 3 \\ & ⇒ & t\dfrac{1}{2} = 1day\end{cases}$

The initial and the final mass of the radioactive element are related by

$\dfrac{m}{{m}_{0}} = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\dfrac{t '}{{t}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}} . . . \left(3\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (3) and solve to calculate the initial mass of the substance.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{8 \times {10}^{- 3}kg}{{m}_{0}} & = & \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\dfrac{5}{1} \\ & ⇒ & {m}_{0} = {2}^{5} \times 8 \times {10}^{- 3}kg \\ & = & 256g\end{cases}$

43698.subject: Physics
43698.text: A steel rod of length $1m$ and cross-sectional area ${10}^{- 4}{m}^{2}$ is heated from $0 ° C$ to $200 ° C$ without being allowed to extend or bend. The compressive tension produced in the rod is _____$\times {10}^{4}N$. (Given Young's modulus of steel $= 2 \times {10}^{11}N{m}^{- 2}$, coefficient of linear expansion $= {10}^{- 5}{K}^{- 1}$ )
43698.sol:
The formula to calculate the Young's modulus of the material of the wire is given by

$Y = \dfrac{FL}{A ∆ L} . . . \left(1\right)$

The increase in length of the wire due to increase in temperature is given by

$∆ L = L\alpha\left({T}_{2} - {T}_{1}\right) . . . \left(2\right)$

Substitute the expression for the extension in length from equation (2) into equation (1) and simplify to obtain the required compressive tension.

$\begin{cases}Y & = & \dfrac{FL}{AL\alpha\left({T}_{2} - {T}_{1}\right)} \\ & ⇒ & F = A\alphaY\left({T}_{2} - {T}_{1}\right) . . . \left(3\right)\end{cases}$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (3) to calculate the required compressive tension in the wire.

$\begin{cases}F & = & {10}^{- 4}{m}^{2} \times {10}^{- 5}{K}^{- 1} \times 2 \times {10}^{11}{Nm}^{- 2} \times \left(200 ° C - 0 ° C\right) \\ & = & 4 \times {10}^{4}N\end{cases}$

43703.subject: Physics
43703.text:
Heat energy of $184kJ$ is given to ice of mass $600g$ at $- 12 ° C$, Specific heat of ice is $2222 . 3J{kg}^{– 1} ° {C}^{– 1}$ and latent heat of ice is $336kJ{kg}^{– 1}$.

(A) Final temperature of system will be $0 ° C$

(B) Final temperature of the system will be greater than $0 ° C$

(C) The final system will have a mixture of ice and water in the ratio of $5: 1$

(D) The final system will have a mixture of ice and water in the ratio of $1: 5$

(E) The final system will have water only

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
43703.sol:
Given:

$∆ Q = 184 \times {10}^{3}J$,

$m = 0 . 600kg\text{at} - 12 ° C$,

$S = 2222 . 3J{kg}^{– 1} ° {C}^{– 1}$ and

$L = 336 \times {10}^{3}J{kg}^{- 1}$

Heat required to convert ice from $– 12 ° C$ to ice at $0 ° C$ will be,

${Q}_{1} = 0 . 600 \times 2222 . 3 \times 12 = 16000 . 56J$

Remaining heat $Q = 184000 - 16000 . 56$

$= 167999 . 44J$

Heat required to melt ice completely at $0 ° C$,

${Q}_{2} = 0 . 600 \times 336000 = 201600J$ needed which is more than $Q$, so $100 %$ ice is not melted.

For amount of melted ice, we can write

$167999 . 44 = m \times 336000 ⇒ m = 0 . 4999kg$

$∴$ mass of water $= 0 . 4999kg$

Mass of ice remaining $= 0 . 1001$

$∴$ Ratio $= \dfrac{0 . 1001}{0 . 4999} \approx 1: 5$

$\dfrac{1}{4} = 1 - \dfrac{{T}_{L}}{{T}_{H}}$

$2η = \dfrac{1}{2} = 1 - \dfrac{{T}_{L} - 58}{{T}_{H}}$
$\dfrac{{T}_{L} - 58}{{T}_{H}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$
$\dfrac{{T}_{L}}{{T}_{L} - 58} = \dfrac{3 / 4}{1 / 2}$
$2{T}_{L} = 3{T}_{L} - 174$
${T}_{L} = 174K$

44560.subject: Physics
44560.text: A spherical ball of mass $2$ kg falls from a height of $10$ m and is brought to rest after penetrating $10$ cm into sand. The average force exerted by sand on the ball is _______ N. (Take $g = 10$ m/s$^2$)
44560.sol:
Using the work-energy theorem, the total work done on the ball is equal to its change in kinetic energy.

Since the ball starts from rest and finally comes to rest, the change in kinetic energy is zero.

$W_{\text{gravity}} + W_{\text{sand}} = \Delta K = 0$

The work done by gravity is over the total distance $h + d$, and the work done by the resistive force of the sand $F$ is over the distance $d$.

$mg(h + d) - Fd = 0$

$F = \dfrac{mg(h + d)}{d}$

Given $m = 2$ kg, $g = 10$ m/s$^2$, $h = 10$ m, and $d = 10$ cm $= 0.1$ m:

$F = \dfrac{2 \times 10 \times (10 + 0.1)}{0.1}$

$F = \dfrac{20 \times 10.1}{0.1}$

$F = 20 \times 101 = 2020$ N

Answer: $2020$

According to Hugo de Vries, evolution is caused by sudden, large, and inheritable changes called mutations.

He believed that mutations are random and directionless, unlike Darwinian variations which are small and directional.

De Vries termed the process of speciation through a single-step large mutation as saltation.

Answer: Single-step large mutation

48455.subject: Chemistry
48455.text: Which of the following is a correct statement for a thermodynamic system?
options: The internal energy changes in all processes
Internal energy and entropy are state functions
The work done in an adiabatic process is always zero
48455.sol:
Internal energy (U$) and entropy (S$) depend only on the initial and final states of the system and are independent of the path followed. Therefore, they are state functions.

Internal energy does not change in an isothermal process for an ideal gas or in a cyclic process, so it does not change in all processes.

Work and heat are path functions, not state functions.

In an adiabatic process, the heat exchange is zero (q = 0$), but the work done is not necessarily zero since \Delta U = w$.

Thus, the only correct statement is that internal energy and entropy are state functions.

Answer: Internal energy and entropy are state functions

48578.subject: Mathematics
48578.text: The area of the region bounded by the curve $y^2 = x^3$, the $y$-axis and the lines $y = 1$ and $y = 8$ is
48578.sol:
The equation of the curve is given by $y^2 = x^3$, which can be written as $x = y^{2/3}$.

The required area is bounded by the curve $x = y^{2/3}$, the $y$-axis ($x = 0$), and the horizontal lines $y = 1$ and $y = 8$.

The area $A$ is given by the definite integral with respect to $y$:

$A = \int_{1}^{8} x \, dy$

Substituting $x = y^{2/3}$:

$A = \int_{1}^{8} y^{2/3} \, dy$

Integrating the function:

$A = \left[ \dfrac{y^{5/3}}{5/3} \right]_{1}^{8}$

$A = \dfrac{3}{5} \left[ y^{5/3} \right]_{1}^{8}$

Evaluating the limits:

$A = \dfrac{3}{5} \left( 8^{5/3} - 1^{5/3} \right)$

Since $8^{5/3} = (2^3)^{5/3} = 2^5 = 32$ and $1^{5/3} = 1$:

$A = \dfrac{3}{5} (32 - 1)$

$A = \dfrac{3}{5} \times 31 = \dfrac{93}{5}$ sq. units.

Answer: $\dfrac{93}{5}$ sq. units

49876.subject: Physics
49876.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I: The resistivity of a conductor is independent of its temperature.
Statement-II: The resistivity of a semiconductor decreases with increase in temperature.
Select the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
49876.sol:
The resistivity of a conductor increases with an increase in temperature due to an increase in the collision frequency of free electrons with the lattice ions. Thus, Statement-I is false.

The resistivity of a semiconductor decreases with an increase in temperature because the number density of charge carriers (electrons and holes) increases exponentially with temperature, which dominates over the effect of increased collision frequency. Thus, Statement-II is true.

Therefore, Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

Answer: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

51052.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
51052.text: The atomic radii of $\mathrm{Li}, \mathrm{F}, \mathrm{Na}$ and Si follow the order.
51052.sol:
Among the given elements Li and Na belong to group 1, i.e. they are alkali metals. So, they will have maximum atomic radii. Between Li and Na, Na will have the largest atomic radii. This is because as we move down the group atomic radii increases.
Si belongs to group 14 and \($\mathrm{F}$\) belongs to group 17 . So, as we move from left to right in period the atomic radii decreases. Thus, Si will have large atomic radii than \($\mathrm{F}$\) but less than Li.
So, the correct order of atomic radii of given elements is, Na > Li > Si > F.

Alkyl halides react with alcoholic silver cyanide ($\text{AgCN}$) to form alkyl isocyanides as the major product.

$\text{AgCN}$ is predominantly covalent in nature, so only the nitrogen atom has a lone pair of electrons available for nucleophilic attack. This leads to the formation of an alkyl isocyanide ($\text{RNC}$).

56016.subject: Chemistry
56016.text: Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding order of reaction?
options: It is not influenced by stoichiometric coefficient of reactants.
It is sum of power to the concentration terms of reactants in rate law equation.
56016.sol:
The order of a reaction, an experimentally determined quantity, specifies how the rate depends on reactant concentrations.

A. The order must be determined experimentally, as it is not generally predictable from stoichiometric coefficients.

B. The stoichiometric coefficients do not influence the order, which may differ from them in complex reactions.

C. The overall order is the sum of the exponents on the concentration terms in the rate law: for $\text{Rate} = k[A]^x[B]^y$, it is $x + y$.

D. Orders are not necessarily whole numbers; they can be fractional, as in the $1.5$ order for acetaldehyde decomposition or the fractional order in $\text{H}_2 + \text{Br}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{HBr}$.

Only D is incorrect.

56051.subject: Chemistry
56051.text:
If a reaction occurs in following two steps
i) $2 \mathrm{ClO}^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{ClO}_2^{-}$
ii) $\mathrm{ClO}_2^{-}+\mathrm{ClO}^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{ClO}_3^{-}+\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$
Find the reaction intermediate.
56051.sol:
A reaction intermediate is a species formed in one elementary step and consumed in a subsequent step, not appearing in the overall balanced equation.

Analyzing the given mechanism:

Step i: $2 \mathrm{ClO}^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{ClO}_2^{-}$

Step ii: $\mathrm{ClO}_2^{-} + \mathrm{ClO}^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{ClO}_3^{-} + \mathrm{Cl}^{-}$

$\mathrm{ClO}_2^{-}$ is produced in step i and consumed in step ii, satisfying the definition of an intermediate.

Summing the steps confirms this:

$2 \mathrm{ClO}^{-} + \mathrm{ClO}_2^{-} + \mathrm{ClO}^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{ClO}_2^{-} + \mathrm{ClO}_3^{-} + \mathrm{Cl}^{-}$

Canceling $\mathrm{ClO}_2^{-}$ from both sides yields the overall equation:

$3 \mathrm{ClO}^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{ClO}_3^{-} + \mathrm{Cl}^{-}$

57601.subject: Chemistry
57601.text: Which of the following is NOT obtained when mixture of methyl bromide and ethyl bromide is treated with sodium metal in presence of dry ether?
57601.sol:
Wurtz reaction of alkyl halides with sodium in dry ether yields alkanes via self-coupling and cross-coupling. For methyl bromide ($\mathrm{CH_3Br}$) and ethyl bromide ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2 Br}$), the products arise from three distinct pathways.

Self-coupling of methyl bromide: $2\mathrm{CH_3Br} + 2\mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{CH_3CH_3} + 2\mathrm{NaBr}$, yielding ethane.

Self-coupling of ethyl bromide: $2\mathrm{CH_3CH_2 Br} + 2\mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_3} + 2\mathrm{NaBr}$, yielding butane.

Cross-coupling: $\mathrm{CH_3Br} + \mathrm{CH_3CH_2 Br} + 2\mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_3} + 2\mathrm{NaBr}$, yielding propane.

The alkanes obtained are ethane, propane, and butane. Pentane is not formed.

58615.subject: Chemistry
58615.text: What is oxidation state of chlorine in chlorous acid?
58615.sol:
The chemical formula of chlorous acid is $HClO_2$.

Let the oxidation state of chlorine be $x$.

The oxidation state of hydrogen is $+1$ and that of oxygen is $-2$.

Since the molecule is neutral, the sum of the oxidation states of all atoms is zero.

$+1 + x + 2(-2) = 0$

$1 + x - 4 = 0$

$x - 3 = 0$

$x = +3$

The oxidation state of chlorine in chlorous acid is $+3$.

Answer: $+3$

58630.subject: Chemistry
58630.text: Which of the following species acts as strongest oxidising agent?
58630.sol:
The strongest oxidizing agent is the species with the greatest tendency to gain electrons, undergoing reduction itself.

Lithium metal ($\mathrm{Li}$) readily loses electrons as a strong reducing agent, not an oxidizing one.

The lithium ion ($\mathrm{Li}^{+}$) possesses a stable electron configuration and minimal tendency for further reduction.

Fluorine gas ($\mathrm{F}_2$) exhibits the strongest electron affinity due to its extreme electronegativity, accepting electrons via $\mathrm{F}_2 + 2\mathrme^{-} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{F}^{-}$ to achieve noble gas stability.

The fluoride ion ($\mathrm{F}^{-}$) is already reduced and shows negligible oxidizing capability.

Among these, $\mathrm{F}_2$ is unequivocally the strongest oxidizing agent.

58792.subject: Chemistry
58792.text: A metal has a fcc structure if the edge length of unit cell is 200 pm, calculate the volume occupied by particles in a unit cell.
58792.sol:
Edge length of the unit cell, $a = 200 \text{ pm} = 2 \times 10^{-8} \text{ cm}$

Volume of the unit cell, $V = a^3 = (2 \times 10^{-8})^3 = 8 \times 10^{-24} \text{ cm}^3$

For a face-centered cubic (fcc) structure, the packing efficiency is $74\%$.

Volume occupied by particles in the unit cell = $0.74 \times V$

$= 0.74 \times 8 \times 10^{-24} \text{ cm}^3$

$= 5.92 \times 10^{-24} \text{ cm}^3$

Answer: $5.92 \times 10^{-24}\ \text{cm}^3$

59417.text: Calculate the number of $\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$ ion in 222 g anhydrous calcium chloride? (At. mass $\mathrm{Ca}=40, \mathrm{Cl}=35 \cdot 5$ )
59417.sol:
Calculating $\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$ ions in 222 g of $\mathrm{CaCl}_2$

The molar mass of $\mathrm{CaCl}_2$ is calculated from atomic masses: $\mathrm{Ca} = 40$ g/mol, $\mathrm{Cl} = 35.5$ g/mol.
$\mathrm{CaCl}_2 = 40 + 2 \times 35.5 = 111$ g/mol

Each mole of $\mathrm{CaCl}_2$ contains 1 mole of $\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$ ions, giving 2 moles of $\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$ ions.

59537.subject: Chemistry
59537.text: A mixture of 0.5 mol $\text{N}_2$ gas, 1.0 mol $\text{O}_2$ gas and 1.5 mol $\text{H}_2$ gas exerts a total pressure of 18 bar. Find the partial pressure of $\text{O}_{2(g)}$.
59537.sol:
Total number of moles in the mixture is:

$n_{total} = n_{N_2} + n_{O_2} + n_{H_2}$

$n_{total} = 0.5 + 1.0 + 1.5 = 3.0$ mol

Mole fraction of $\text{O}_2$ is:

$x_{O_2} = \dfrac{n_{O_2}}{n_{total}} = \dfrac{1.0}{3.0} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

According to Dalton's law of partial pressures, the partial pressure of $\text{O}_2$ is:

$P_{O_2} = x_{O_2} \times P_{total}$

$P_{O_2} = \dfrac{1}{3} \times 18 = 6.0$ bar

Answer: $6.0$ bar

61258.subject: Mathematics
61258.text: $The order and degree of the differential equation \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{1}{\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2}} = \left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}$, respectively are
61258.sol:
The given differential equation is $\sqrt{1 + \dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2}} = \left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^{\dfrac{3}{2}}$

Squaring both sides to remove the fractional powers, we get:

$1 + \dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2} = \left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^3$

Multiplying the entire equation by $\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2$ to express it as a polynomial in derivatives:

$\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + 1 = \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 \left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^3$

The highest order derivative present in the equation is $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$, which means the order of the differential equation is $2$.

The power of the highest order derivative in this polynomial form is $3$, which means the degree of the differential equation is $3$.

Therefore, the order and degree are $2$ and $3$, respectively.

Answer: $2, 3$

62203.text: If $\int \frac{e^x}{\sqrt{\mathrme^{2 x}+4 \mathrm{e}^x+13}} d x=\log \left|e^{a x}+2+\sqrt{\mathrme^{2 x}+4 \mathrm{e}^x+13}\right|+\mathrm{c}$, (where c is the constant of integration), then the value of $a$ is equal to
62203.sol:
Evaluate the integral $I = \int \frac{e^x}{\sqrt{e^{2x}+4e^x+13}}\,dx$ for which the solution is asserted to equal $\log\left|e^{ax}+2+\sqrt{e^{2x}+4e^x+13}\right|+c$, and determine constant $a$.

Substitute with $t = e^x$, hence $dt = e^x\,dx$. The integral simplifies to $I = \int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{t^2+4t+13}}$.

The quadratic expression $t^2+4t+13$ is restructured by completing the square to $(t+2)^{2}+9 = (t+2)^{2}+3^{2}$, so $I = \int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{(t+2)^{2}+3^{2}}}$.

Using the standard form $\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{x^{2}+a^{2}}}=\log\left|x+\sqrt{x^{2}+a^{2}}\right|+C$, where $x = t+2$ and $a=3$, integrate to obtain $I = \log\left|(t+2)+\sqrt{(t+2)^{2}+3^{2}}\right|+C$.

Substitute back $t = e^x$ to yield $I = \log\left|(e^x+2)+\sqrt{(e^x+2)^{2}+9}\right|+C = \log\left|e^x+2+\sqrt{e^{2x}+4e^x+13}\right|+C$.

Comparing with the provided expression $\log\left|e^{ax}+2+\sqrt{e^{2x}+4e^x+13}\right|+c$, we conclude $e^{ax} = e^x$ and therefore $a=1$.

Final answer: $\boxed{1}$

65140.text: If $4 \hat{i}+7 \hat{j}+8 \hat{k}, 2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}+4 \hat{k}$ and $2 \hat{i}+5 \hat{j}+7 \hat{k}$ are the position vectors of the vertices $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}$ and C , respectively, of triangle ABC , then the position vector of the point in which bisector of $\angle B$ meets $C A$ is
65140.sol:
Given:
$\mathrm{a} = 4\hat{i} + 7\hat{j} + 8\hat{k}$
$\mathrm{b} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$
$\mathrm{c} = 2\hat{i} + 5\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}$

Vectors from vertex B:
$\mathrm{BA} = \mathrm{a} - \mathrm{b} = 2\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$
$\mathrm{BC} = \mathrm{c} - \mathrm{b} = 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$

Magnitudes:
$|\mathrm{BA}| = \sqrt{2^2 + 4^2 + 4^2} = 6$
$|\mathrm{BC}| = \sqrt{2^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{13}$

By the Angle Bisector Theorem, point D divides AC in the ratio $|\mathrm{BA}| : |\mathrm{BC}| = 6 : \sqrt{13}$.

Applying the section formula:
$\mathrm{d} = \frac{\sqrt{13} \cdot \mathrm{a} + 6 \cdot \mathrm{c}}{\sqrt{13} + 6}$

Substituting the given vectors:
$\mathrm{d} = \frac{(4\sqrt{13} + 12)\hat{i} + (7\sqrt{13} + 30)\hat{j} + (8\sqrt{13} + 42)\hat{k}}{\sqrt{13} + 6}$

This expression corresponds to option C.

65184.subject: Mathematics
65184.text: The maximum value and minimum value of the volume of the parallelopiped having coterminous edges $\hat{i}+x \hat{j}+\hat{\mathrm{k}}, \hat{\mathrm{j}}+x \hat{\mathrm{k}}$ and $x \hat{i}+\hat{\mathrm{k}}$ are respectively
65184.sol:
The volume $V$ of the parallelepiped with coterminous edges $\mathrm{a} = \hat{i}+x \hat{j}+\hat{k}$, $\mathrm{b} = \hat{j}+x \hat{k}$, and $\mathrm{c} = x \hat{i}+\hat{k}$ is given by the scalar triple product:

$V(x) = |[\mathrm{a} \mathrm{b} \mathrm{c}]| = \left| \begin{vmatrix} 1 \text{ and } x \text{ and } 1 \ 0 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } x \ x \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } 1 \end{vmatrix} \right|$

Evaluating the determinant yields $V(x) = |x^3 - x + 1|$.

To find the extrema of $V(x)$, consider $f(x) = x^3 - x + 1$ since both critical values are positive. The derivative $f'(x) = 3x^2 - 1$ vanishes at $x = \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$.

The second derivative $f''(x) = 6x$ shows $f(x)$ has a local minimum at $x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ and a local maximum at $x = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$.

At these points:

$f\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = 1 - \frac{2}{3\sqrt{3}}$

$f\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = 1 + \frac{2}{3\sqrt{3}}$

Both values are positive, so $V(x)$ attains these values directly.

Maximum volume: $1 + \frac{2}{3\sqrt{3}}$

Minimum volume: $1 - \frac{2}{3\sqrt{3}}$

These correspond to option B.

66780.subject: Physics
66780.text:
A long rectangular conducting loop of width '$l$' mass '$m$' and resistance '$R$' is placed partly in a perpendicular magnetic field '$B$'. With what velocity should it be pushed downwards so that it may continue to fall without any acceleration? (g$ = acceleration due to gravity)
$
66780.sol:
When the loop falls with a velocity $v$, the motional emf induced in the top horizontal segment of the loop is given by:

$\varepsilon = Bvl$

The induced current in the loop is:

$I = \dfrac{\varepsilon}{R} = \dfrac{Bvl}{R}$

This current experiences an upward magnetic force due to the magnetic field $B$. The magnitude of this force is:

$F_m = IlB = \left(\dfrac{Bvl}{R}\right)lB = \dfrac{B^2l^2v}{R}$

For the loop to fall without any acceleration, the net force on it must be zero. Therefore, the upward magnetic force must balance the downward gravitational force:

$F_m = mg$

$\dfrac{B^2l^2v}{R} = mg$

Solving for $v$, we get:

$v = \dfrac{mgR}{B^2l^2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{mgR}{B^2 l^2}$

67687.subject: Physics
67687.text: The relation between magnetic moment $(\mathrm{M})$ of a current carrying circular coil and length (L) of the wire used is
67687.sol:
The magnetic moment of a circular coil with N turns carrying current I is expressed as $M = NIA$, where $A = \pi r^2$ is the area per turn.

Given a fixed wire length $L = N(2\pi r)$, the radius is determined by $r = \frac{L}{2\pi N}$.

Substituting into the area formula yields $A = \pi \left(\frac{L}{2\pi N}\right)^2 = \frac{L^2}{4\pi N^2}$.

Thus, the magnetic moment becomes $M = NI \cdot \frac{L^2}{4\pi N^2} = \frac{I L^2}{4\pi N}$.

For constant I and N, $M \propto L^2$, indicating direct proportionality to the square of the wire length.

The correct choice is $\boxed{\text{C}}$.

67991.text: The percentage error in the measurement of mass of a body and its speed are $0.73\%$ and $1.84\%$ respectively. The percentage error in the measurement of its momentum and kinetic energy are respectively
67991.sol:
Given percentage error in mass, $\dfrac{\Delta m}{m} \times 100 = 0.73\%$

Given percentage error in speed, $\dfrac{\Delta v}{v} \times 100 = 1.84\%$

Momentum is given by $p = mv$

Percentage error in momentum is $\dfrac{\Delta p}{p} \times 100 = \dfrac{\Delta m}{m} \times 100 + \dfrac{\Delta v}{v} \times 100$

$\dfrac{\Delta p}{p} \times 100 = 0.73\% + 1.84\% = 2.57\%$

Kinetic energy is given by $K = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2$

Percentage error in kinetic energy is $\dfrac{\Delta K}{K} \times 100 = \dfrac{\Delta m}{m} \times 100 + 2\dfrac{\Delta v}{v} \times 100$

$\dfrac{\Delta K}{K} \times 100 = 0.73\% + 2(1.84\%) = 0.73\% + 3.68\% = 4.41\%$

Answer: $2.57\%$ , $4.41\%$

68147.subject: Physics
68147.text: Let $R_1, R_2$ and $R_3$ be the radii of three mercury drops. $A$ big mercury drop is formed from them under isothermal conditions. The radius of the resultant drop is
68147.sol:
Volume Conservation Principle

Under isothermal conditions with constant density, the total volume remains conserved during the coalescence of three mercury drops. The volume of each spherical drop is $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3$.

The combined volume of the small drops with radii $R_1$, $R_2$, and $R_3$ equals the volume of the resultant drop with radius $R$:

$\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi R_1^3 + \frac{4}{3}\pi R_2^3 + \frac{4}{3}\pi R_3^3$

Simplifying, we factor out the common term:

$R^3 = R_1^3 + R_2^3 + R_3^3$

Taking the cube root of both sides, the radius of the big drop is:

$R = \left(R_1^3 + R_2^3 + R_3^3\right)^{1/3}$

This corresponds to option A.

68705.subject: Physics
68705.text:
The motion of the particle is given by the equation $x=A \sin \omega t+B \cos \omega t$.
The motion of the particle is
68705.sol:
The equation of motion $x = A \sin \omega t + B \cos \omega t$ represents the superposition of two simple harmonic motions with identical angular frequency $\omega$.

This expression can be transformed into the standard simple harmonic form $x = R \sin(\omega t + \phi)$ by applying the trigonometric identity $\sin(X + Y) = \sin X \cos Y + \cos X \sin Y$, yielding $x = R \sin \omega t \cos \phi + R \cos \omega t \sin \phi$.

Matching coefficients with the original equation gives $A = R \cos \phi$ and $B = R \sin \phi$.

Squaring and adding these equations results in $A^2 + B^2 = R^2 \cos^2 \phi + R^2 \sin^2 \phi = R^2(\cos^2 \phi + \sin^2 \phi) = R^2$, since $\cos^2 \phi + \sin^2 \phi = 1$.

Therefore, the amplitude is $R = (A^2 + B^2)^{1/2}$, confirming the motion is simple harmonic with this amplitude.

The correct choice is $\boxed{C}$.

69590.text: Which one of the following graph represents forward bias characteristic of a diode?
69590.sol:
Conceptual problem. Theory based.
Graph D has exponential characteristic, which is similar to ideal diode.

The current-voltage function (also called the " $i-v$ characteristic") for an ideal diode is
$i(v)=I_S\left[\exp \left(\frac{v}{\eta V_T}\right)-1\right], v>V_Z$
where $I_S$ is the reverse saturation current, $v$ is the applied voltage (reverse bias is negative), $V_T$ is constant dependent on temperature, and $\eta$ is the emission coefficient, which is 1 for germanium devices and 2 for silicon devices.
$V_Z$ is the reverse bias break done voltage.

70162.sol:
According to Rayleigh's criterion, the angular separation between two point sources just resolved by a telescope is given by $\Delta \theta = \dfrac{1.22 \lambda}{D}$, where $\lambda$ is the wavelength of light and $D$ is the diameter of the objective lens.

The linear distance $x$ between the centres of their diffraction patterns in the focal plane of the lens is given by:

$x = f \Delta \theta = \dfrac{1.22 \lambda f}{D}$

Given:
$D = 5$ cm
$f = 25$ cm
$\lambda = 5000$ \AA

Substituting the given values:

$ x = \dfrac{1.22 \times 5000 \text{ \AA} \times 25 \text{ cm}}{5 \text{ cm}}$

$x = 1.22 \times 5000 \times 5$ \AA

$ x = 6.1 \times 5000$ \AA

$ x = 30500$ \AA

Answer: $30500$ Å

70947.subject: Biology
70947.text: Various properties of water are due to ____________ between water molecules.
70947.sol:
Water molecules are polar in nature, with the oxygen atom being partially negative and the hydrogen atoms being partially positive. This polarity allows the formation of intermolecular hydrogen bonds between adjacent water molecules.

These hydrogen bonds are responsible for various unique properties of water, such as its high boiling point, high specific heat capacity, high surface tension, and its ability to act as a universal solvent.

Peptide bonds are found in proteins, glycosidic bonds in carbohydrates, and disulphide bonds in proteins.

Answer: hydrogen bonds

71139.subject: Biology
71139.text: Pneumonitis and Eosinophilia are symptoms of __________.
71139.sol:
Ascariasis is an infection caused by the roundworm Ascaris lumbricoides. During its life cycle, the larvae migrate through the lungs, which can cause an inflammatory response known as Ascaris pneumonitis (Loeffler's syndrome). This condition is typically accompanied by a marked increase in eosinophils in the blood, known as eosinophilia.

Amoebiasis primarily affects the intestines and liver. Typhoid is a bacterial infection causing high fever and intestinal issues. Nasopharyngitis is a viral infection of the upper respiratory tract (common cold).

Answer: Ascariasis

71774.text: What is the cell constant of a cell containing a solution of resistance $90$ Ohm with conductivity $2 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{Ohm}^{-1}\text{cm}^{-1}$?
71774.sol:
The cell constant $G^*$ is related to conductivity $\kappa$ and resistance $R$ by the formula:

$G^* = \kappa \times R$

Given:
$\kappa = 2 \times 10^{-3}\ \Omega^{-1}\text{cm}^{-1}$
$R = 90\ \Omega$

Substituting the values:

$G^* = (2 \times 10^{-3}) \times 90$

$G^* = 180 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{cm}^{-1}$

$G^* = 0.18\ \text{cm}^{-1}$

Answer: $0.18\ \text{cm}^{-1}$

71922.subject: Chemistry
71922.text: Predict the oxidation number of of 'C' in $\text{K}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4$ and in $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$.
71922.sol:
Let the oxidation number of $\text{C}$ in $\text{K}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4$ be $x$.

The oxidation number of $\text{K}$ is $+1$ and $\text{O}$ is $-2$.

$2(+1) + 2x + 4(-2) = 0$

$2 + 2x - 8 = 0$

$2x = 6 \Rightarrow x = +3$

Let the oxidation number of $\text{C}$ in $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$ be $y$.

The oxidation number of $\text{H}$ is $+1$ and $\text{Cl}$ is $-1$.

$y + 2(+1) + 2(-1) = 0$

$y + 2 - 2 = 0 \Rightarrow y = 0$

72162.subject: Physics
72162.text: When light of wavelength '$\lambda$' is incident on a photosensitive surface, the stopping potential is '$V$'. When light of wavelength '$2\lambda$' is incident on the same surface, the stopping potential is $V/3$. Threshold wavelength for the surface is
72162.sol:
Using Einstein's photoelectric equation:

$eV = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \phi$

$\dfrac{eV}{3} = \dfrac{hc}{2\lambda} - \phi$

Multiplying the second equation by $3$:

$eV = \dfrac{3hc}{2\lambda} - 3\phi$

Equating the two expressions for $eV$:

$\dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \phi = \dfrac{3hc}{2\lambda} - 3\phi$

$2\phi = \dfrac{3hc}{2\lambda} - \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$

$2\phi = \dfrac{hc}{2\lambda}$

$\phi = \dfrac{hc}{4\lambda}$

The work function is given by $\phi = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0}$, where $\lambda_0$ is the threshold wavelength.

$\dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0} = \dfrac{hc}{4\lambda}$

$\lambda_0 = 4\lambda$

Answer: $4\lambda$

72366.subject: Physics
72366.text: Out of the following what is used to detect the intensity of light ?
72366.sol:
A photodiode is a p-n junction diode fabricated with a transparent window to allow light to fall on the diode.

It is operated under reverse bias. When the photodiode is illuminated with light (photons) with energy greater than the energy gap of the semiconductor, electron-hole pairs are generated due to the absorption of photons.

Due to the electric field of the junction, electrons and holes are separated before they recombine. The magnitude of the photocurrent is directly proportional to the intensity of incident light.

Thus, a photodiode in reverse bias is used to detect the intensity of light.

Answer: Photodiode in reverse bias

73806.subject: General Ability
73806.text: A periscope uses two plane mirrors inclined at $45^{}^{\circ}$. If the tube of the periscope is filled with a complete transparent liquid of refractive index $1.5$, then which one of the following is correct in respect of the image seen?
options: The image will appear laterally shifted.
The image will appear $1.5$ times brighter.
The image will appear $1.5$ times darker.
73806.sol:
The working of a periscope is based on the successive reflections of light from two plane mirrors placed parallel to each other and inclined at an angle of $45^{}^{\circ}$.

The image formation by a plane mirror is governed by the laws of reflection, which state that the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection. These laws are entirely independent of the refractive index of the surrounding medium.

When the tube of the periscope is filled with a completely transparent liquid of refractive index $1.5$, the light rays entering normally will undergo reflection at the same angles (45^{}^{\circ}$) as they would in air. Since the liquid is completely transparent, there is no absorption of light, meaning the brightness of the image will not be altered by a factor of 1.5$.

Because the geometry of reflection remains unaffected by the change in the medium, the position, size, and nature of the image will remain unchanged.

76779.subject: Mathematics
76779.text:
Consider the function
$f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{ccc}
\frac{\alpha \cos x}{\pi-2 x} & \text{ If } & x \neq \frac{\pi}{2} \\
3 & \text{ If } & x=\frac{\pi}{2}
\end{array}\right.$
Which is continuous at $x=\frac{\pi}{2}$, where $\alpha$ is a constant.
What is the value of $\alpha$ ?
76779.sol:
$f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{ccc}
\frac{\alpha \cos x}{\pi-2 x} & \text{ if } & x \neq \frac{\pi}{2} \\
3 & \text{ if } & x=\frac{\pi}{2}
\end{array}\right.$
For continuity at $\mathrm{x}=\frac{\pi}{2}\text{ L.H.L. }=\lim _{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi^{-}}{2}} f(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi^{-}}{2}} \frac{\alpha \cos x}{\pi-2 x}$
Put $\mathrm{x}=\frac{\pi}{2}-\mathrm{h}$ where $\mathrm{x} \rightarrow \frac{\pi}{2}$, then $\mathrm{h} \rightarrow 0\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \quad \text{ L.H.L. }=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{\alpha \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-h\right)}{\pi-2\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-h\right)}=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{\alpha \sin h}{\pi-\pi+2 h} \\
& {\left[\because \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\theta\right)=\sin \theta\right]} \\
& =\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{2 \alpha \sin h}{2 h}=\frac{\alpha}{2} \lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sin h}{h} \\
& =\frac{\alpha}{2} \cdot 1=\frac{\alpha}{2} \quad\left[\because \lim _{\theta \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sin \theta}{\theta}=1\right] \\
& \text{ and R.H.L. }=\lim _{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi^{+}}{2}} f(x) \lim _{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi^{+}}{2}} \frac{\alpha \cos x}{\pi-2 \pi}
\end{aligned}$
Put $\mathrm{x}=\frac{\pi}{2}+\mathrm{h}$ when $\mathrm{x} \rightarrow \frac{\pi}{2}$, then $\mathrm{h} \rightarrow 0\therefore \quad \text{ R.H.L. }=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{\alpha \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}+h\right)}{\pi-2\left(\frac{\pi}{2}+h\right)}=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{\alpha(-\sin h)}{\pi-\pi-2 h}\begin{array}{ll}
=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0}-\frac{\alpha \sin h}{-2 h} & {\left[\because \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}+\theta\right)=-\sin \theta\right]} \\
=\frac{\alpha}{2} \lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sin h}{h}=\frac{\alpha}{2} & \left(\because \lim _{\theta \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sin \theta}{\theta}=1\right)
\end{array}
Also, \mathrm{f}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=3$
Since, $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=\frac{\pi}{2}\begin{aligned}$& \therefore \quad $\text{ L.H.L. }=\text{ R.H.L. }=\mathrm{f} \left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\\ \text{ and } \quad \frac{\alpha}{2}=\frac{\alpha}{2}=3 \\ \text{ and } \quad \alpha=6
\end{aligned}$
Hence, for $\alpha=6$, the given function ( f ) is continuous
$\text{ at }}x=\frac{\pi}{2}$

& \therefore \mathrm{p}_3=\sqrt{(12)^2+(16)^2} \\
& =\sqrt{144+256} \\
& =20 \mathrm{~kg}-\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}

The sum of total inhibitory environmental factors, both biotic and abiotic, which regulate population size and do not permit unlimited growth of population is called environmental resistance. Because of environmental resistance, the populations are unable to reach full biotic potential.

84930.subject: Zoology
84930.text: Which of the following best illustrates "feedback" in development?
options: Tissue $\mathrm{X}$ secretes RNA which changes the development of tissue Y.
As tissue $\mathrm{X}$ develops, it secretes enzymes that inhibit the development of tissue $Y$.
As tissue $\mathrm{X}$ develops, it secretes something that induces tissue $\mathrm{Y}$ to develop.
As tissue $\mathrm{X}$ develops, it secretes something that slows down the growth of tissue Y.
84930.sol:
As tissue $\mathrm{X}$ develops, it secrets something that induce tissue $\mathrm{Y}$ to develop indicating positive feedback mechanism.
Related Theory
Feedback mechanism is the mechanism of the body to maintain the levels of hormones in the body in the desired limits. An increase or decrease in the levels of the hormones triggers the feedback mechanism. Whenever there is a change in the normal state, the messages are sent to 'increase' secretions if there is a fall below normal or to 'decrease' secretions if there is a rise above normal to restore the normal body state. Such a mechanism is called a negative feedback mechanism.

85096.subject: Zoology
85096.text: Which of the following is correct for r-selected species?
options: Large number of progeny with small size
Large number of progeny with large size
Small number of progeny with small size
Small number of progeny with large size
85096.sol:
Population evolve to maximize their reproductive fitness in the habitat in which they live. This fitness towards maximizing reproductive is called as Darwinian fitness (high r-value). According to this, under a particular set of selection pressures, organism evolves towards the most efficient reproductive strategy. Some of these are as follows:

(i) BREEDING HABIT: Some organisms breed only once in their lifetime (pacific salmon fish) while others breed many times during their lifetime (most bird and mammals)

(ii) NUMBER AND SIZE OF OFFSPRING: Some produce a large number of small-sized offspring (oysters, pelagic fishes) while others produce a small number of large-sized offspring (birds and animals).

85356.subject: Zoology
85356.text: Pattern baldness, moustaches and beard in human males are examples of:
85356.sol:
Sex-limited traits are traits that are visible only within one sex. Premature baldness and type of beard growth are human sex-limited characters. Sex linked traits are traits that are found on either one of the chromosomes that determine sex, or the sex chromosomes. Examples: haemophilia.
Related Theory
Genes that are located on the sex chromosomes are called as sex linked genes. Because $X$ and $Y$ chromosomes have different genes, sex-linked genes have a pattern of expression that is different from autosomal genes. Because males only have one copy of each type of sex chromosome. they express all of the alleles on both chromosomes. Sex-influenced traits are autosomal traits that are influenced by sex. One such gene is baldness.

85689.subject: Biology
85689.text: There is a difference between the predicted and observed global carbon budget. The possible reason is:
options: Higher $\text{CO}_2$ levels stimulate plant growth and productivity, leading to more carbon being sequestered in plant tissues and root systems.
The thinning of the stratospheric ozone layer allows higher levels of ultraviolet radiation directly breaking down $\text{CO}_2$ molecules.
Oceans are absorbing more carbon due to increased temperature, resulting in increased acidification.
Higher $\text{CO}_2$ levels lead to increased soil respiration rates, releasing more carbon into the atmosphere.
85689.sol:
The difference between the predicted and observed global carbon budget is often referred to as the missing carbon sink. This discrepancy arises because the amount of carbon dioxide accumulating in the atmosphere is less than expected based on human emissions and known ocean uptake.

A primary explanation for this missing sink is the $\text{CO}_2$ fertilization effect. Higher atmospheric $\text{CO}_2$ concentrations stimulate photosynthesis, leading to enhanced plant growth and productivity. Consequently, more carbon is sequestered in terrestrial ecosystems, particularly in plant tissues and root systems, accounting for the unaccounted carbon.

Answer: Higher $\text{CO}_2$ levels stimulate plant growth and productivity, leading to more carbon being sequestered in plant tissues and root systems.

95301.sol: Over time the centre of the innermost layers of the stem gets deposited with organic compounds like tannins, raisins, oils, gums and other aromatic substances. 96795.subject: Botany
96795.text: Match column I with column II and select the CORRECT option from the codes given below.
96795.sol:
Nitrogen is one of the essential macronutrients required by plants and absorbed in the form of nitrates and nitrites. It forms a major constituent of proteins, vitamins, chlorophyll, pyrimidines and hormones. Deficiency of nitrogen of leads to stunted growth, chlorosis, reduced cell division, decrease in protein content, wrinkling of cereal grains, purple coloration of the shoot axis.

Iron is another essential element necessary for plant growth and development. Chlorophyll production requires iron and it is a component of many enzymes which participate in energy transfer, nitrogen fixation, lignification. Iron deficiency is clearly indicated by chlorosis where leaf yellowing appears first in the interveinal regions of the young leaves. Chlorosis referes to production of insufficienct chlorophyll leading to yellowing of the leaves.

Chlorine is absorbed in the form of chloride ions and it helps in maintaining salt balance in cells of plant. Chlorine is important for opening and closing of stomata. Chlorine deficiency results in the wilting of the leaves which later turn in bronze colour.

Boron is another essential element which is required for membrane functioning, pollen germination, cell differentiation. It is also required for calcium uptake and utilization. Boron deficiency symptoms include leaves with yellowish or reddish cast, growing points stop functioning leading to stunted or rosette appearance. Its deficiency also causes formation of cracked fruits.

98387.subject: Chemistry
98387.text: Co-factor and prosthetic groups are __________ compounds, ________ bound to apoenzyme.
98387.sol: Enzymes are proteinaceous in nature. Some Enzymes also contain non-protein part known as Co-factors. These factors are attached to the Enzymes to enhanced their catalytic activity. The protein part of Enzyme is known as Apoenzyme. Hence Apoenzyme (Protein part) + Co-factors (Non protein part) = Holoenzyme (Whole Enzyme). As the co-factors are bound to enzymes, the removal of these factors affects the overall activity of Enzymes too. These co-factors can be organic or inorganic. Organic cofactors if tightly bound are known as Prosthetic groups and if loosely bound are termed as Co-enzymes. The inorganic co-factors are metal ions. Example of inorganic co-factor is Zinc which is a co-factor of enzyme Carboxypeptidase.

101690.subject: Physics
101690.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When an incompressible ideal fluid flows steadily through a horizontal pipe of varying cross-section, the fluid velocity is maximum at the narrowest part of the pipe.
Reason (R): According to Bernoulli's principle, for a steady horizontal flow of an ideal fluid, a region of higher fluid velocity is accompanied by a lower static pressure.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
101690.sol:
Assertion (A) is true: According to the equation of continuity for an incompressible fluid, $A_1v_1 = A_2v_2$. The velocity of the fluid is inversely proportional to the cross-sectional area. Therefore, the fluid velocity is maximum at the narrowest part of the pipe where the area is minimum.

Reason (R) is true: Bernoulli's principle for a horizontal pipe states that $P + \dfrac{1}{2}\rho v^2 = \text{constant}$. This implies that an increase in fluid velocity results in a decrease in static pressure.

However, Reason (R) is not the correct explanation for Assertion (A). The maximum velocity at the narrowest part is a direct consequence of the conservation of mass (equation of continuity), not the conservation of energy (Bernoulli's principle). Therefore, both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) does not explain (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

103924.subject: Physics
103924.text: A branch of an electrical circuit between points M and N contains an ideal inductor of $1 \text{ H}$, a battery of $3 \text{ V}$, and a resistor of $2 \ \Omega$ connected in series. The current flows from M to N. The negative terminal of the battery is connected towards M and the positive terminal towards N. The current $i$ (in A) varies with time $t$ (in s) as a straight line passing through the coordinates $(t=0, i=1)$ and $(t=2, i=5)$ on an $i-t$ graph. What is the potential difference $V_M - V_N$ at $t = 1 \text{ s}$?
103924.sol:
From the given coordinates $(0, 1)$ and $(2, 5)$, the rate of change of current is the slope of the $i-t$ graph:
$\dfrac{di}{dt} = \dfrac{5 - 1}{2 - 0} = 2 \text{ A/s}$

The current at $t = 1 \text{ s}$ can be found from the linear relation $i = 1 + 2t$:
$i = 1 + 2(1) = 3 \text{ A}$

Applying Kirchhoff's Voltage Law from M to N:
$V_M - L\dfrac{di}{dt} + E - iR = V_N$
Note that the battery is traversed from the negative to the positive terminal, so its potential change is $+3 \text{ V}$.

Substituting the values:
$V_M - (1)(2) + 3 - (3)(2) = V_N$
$V_M - 2 + 3 - 6 = V_N$
$V_M - 5 = V_N$
$V_M - V_N = 5 \text{ V}$

Answer: $5 \text{ V}$

104465.subject: Physics
104465.text: Two lenses, A and B, are made of the same transparent material. Lens A is an equiconvex lens, while lens B is a plano-convex lens. If the curved surfaces of both lenses have the same radius of curvature, what is the ratio of the power of lens A to the power of lens B?
104465.sol:
Let the radius of curvature of the curved surfaces be $R$ and the refractive index of the material be $\mu$.

For the equiconvex lens A, the radii of curvature are $R_{1} = R$ and $R_{2} = -R$.
The power of lens A is:
$P_{A} = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{-R}\right) = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{2}{R}\right)$

For the plano-convex lens B, the radii of curvature are $R_{1} = R$ and $R_{2} = \infty$.
The power of lens B is:
$P_{B} = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{\infty}\right) = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R}\right)$

The ratio of their powers is:
$\dfrac{P_{A}}{P_{B}} = \dfrac{2(\mu - 1)/R}{(\mu - 1)/R} = \dfrac{2}{1}$

Thus, the ratio is $2:1$.

Answer: $2:1$

104650.text:
STATEMENT-1 : The two slits in YDSE are illuminated by two different sodium lamps emitting light of same wavelength. No interference pattern will be observed.
STATEMENT - 2 : Two independent light sources (except LASER) cannot be coherent.

104650.sol:
"The two slits in YDSE are illuminated by two different sodium lamps emitting light of same wavelength. No interference pattern will be observed."
Correct. Even though wavelength is same, two independent lamps are not coherent sources (their phase difference keeps changing randomly), so no sustained interference pattern is formed.
Statement-2:
"Two independent light sources (except LASER) cannot be coherent."
\(\leftarrow\) Correct. Coherent sources must maintain a constant phase difference, which is not possible with independent sources (except lasers).
Relation:
Statement-2 correctly explains why Statement-1 is true.

104690.subject: Physics
104690.text: For a given transparent medium with respect to vacuum, the polarizing angle (Brewster's angle) is $i_p$ and the critical angle for total internal reflection is $i_c$. Which of the following is the correct mathematical relation between $i_p$ and $i_c$?
104690.sol:
According to Brewster's law, the refractive index $\mu$ of the medium is related to the polarizing angle $i_p$ by:
$\mu = \tan(i_p)$

The critical angle $i_c$ for total internal reflection for the same medium with respect to vacuum is given by:
$\sin(i_c) = \dfrac{1}{\mu}$

Substituting the value of $\mu$ from the first equation into the second, we get:
$\sin(i_c) = \dfrac{1}{\tan(i_p)}$
$\Rightarrow \sin(i_c) = \cot(i_p)$

Answer: $\sin(i_c) = \cot(i_p)$

113893.subject: Chemistry
113893.text: Air is enclosed over water in a closed vessel at a total pressure of $5.0\text{ atm}$. If the mole fraction of oxygen in the air is $0.20$ and the Henry's law constant ($K_H$) for oxygen in water at the given temperature is $4 \times 10^4\text{ atm}$, what is the mole fraction of oxygen dissolved in the water?
113893.sol:
According to Dalton's law of partial pressures, the partial pressure of oxygen ($p_{\text{O}_2}$) in the gaseous phase is:
$p_{\text{O}_2} = \text{Total pressure} \times \text{Mole fraction of O}_2\text{ in air}$
$p_{\text{O}_2} = 5.0\text{ atm} \times 0.20 = 1.0\text{ atm}$

According to Henry's law, the partial pressure of a gas is directly proportional to its mole fraction ($x$) in the solution:
$p_{\text{O}_2} = K_H \times x_{\text{O}_2}$
$1.0\text{ atm} = (4 \times 10^4\text{ atm}) \times x_{\text{O}_2}$
$x_{\text{O}_2} = \dfrac{1.0}{4 \times 10^4} = 0.25 \times 10^{-4} = 2.5 \times 10^{-5}$

Answer: $2.5 \times 10^{-5}$

117100.subject: Chemistry
117100.text: Which of the following catalyst-reaction pairs is incorrectly matched?
options: Finely divided $\text{Ni}$ : Catalytic hydrogenation of unsaturated hydrocarbons
$\text{Zn}^{2+}$ : Oxidation of iodide to iodine by persulphate
117100.sol:
Transition metals and their compounds act as good catalysts due to their ability to adopt multiple oxidation states and form complexes.

$\text{MnO}_2$ is used as a catalyst in the decomposition of $\text{KClO}_3$ to yield oxygen gas.

$\text{TiCl}_4$ with $\text{Al}(\text{CH}_3)_3$ forms the Ziegler-Natta catalyst, which is used for the polymerisation of ethene.

Finely divided $\text{Ni}$ is widely used as a catalyst in the hydrogenation of unsaturated hydrocarbons (alkenes and alkynes).

The oxidation of iodide to iodine by persulphate is catalysed by $\text{Fe}^{3+}$, not $\text{Zn}^{2+}$. $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ has a completely filled d-orbital ($3d^{10}$) and a fixed +2 oxidation state, so it cannot provide the variable oxidation states required to catalyse this redox reaction.

Thus, the incorrectly matched pair is $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ : Oxidation of iodide to iodine by persulphate.

Answer: $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ : Oxidation of iodide to iodine by persulphate

123414.subject: Botany
123414.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the vertical section of an isobilateral leaf, the vascular bundles are generally seen to be of near similar sizes.
Reason (R): The near similar sizes of vascular bundles in isobilateral leaves is due to the presence of reticulate venation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
123414.sol:
Assertion (A) is true because in isobilateral (monocotyledonous) leaves, the vascular bundles are generally of near similar sizes (except in main veins) as seen in vertical sections.

Reason (R) is false because isobilateral leaves typically possess parallel venation, not reticulate venation. It is this parallel venation that is reflected in the near similar sizes of the vascular bundles. Reticulate venation is a characteristic of dicotyledonous (dorsiventral) leaves, where the vascular bundles vary greatly in size depending on the size of the veins.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

123713.subject: Botany
123713.text: How does the process in Anaphase II in meiosis lead to the movement of sister chromatids toward opposite poles?
options: By the reappearance of the nuclear envelope
By the shortening of microtubules attached to kinetochores
123713.sol: In contrast to meiosis I, meiosis II resembles a normal mitosis. The nuclear membrane disappears by the end of prophase II (Figure 10.4). The chromosomes again become compact. Metaphase II: At this stage the chromosomes align at the equator and the microtubules from opposite poles of the spindle get attached to the kinetochores (Figure 10.4) of sister chromatids. It begins with the simultaneous splitting of the centromere of each chromosome (which was holding the sister chromatids together), allowing them to move toward opposite poles of the cell by shortening of microtubules attached to kinetochores.

124733.subject: Botany
124733.text:
A horticulturist wants to achieve three specific goals in a commercial nursery:
(i) Initiate rooting in stem cuttings to quickly propagate a desired plant.
(ii) Cause apples to elongate and improve their shape.
(iii) Delay the senescence of harvested leaves.

Which of the following sequences of plant growth regulators should be applied to achieve these goals respectively?
124733.sol:
Goal (i): Auxins (such as IBA and NAA) are widely used to initiate rooting in stem cuttings, which is a common application for vegetative plant propagation.

Goal (ii): Gibberellins (GAs) are specifically used to cause fruits like apples to elongate and improve their shape.

Goal (iii): Cytokinins help delay leaf senescence by promoting nutrient mobilisation.

Thus, the correct sequence of plant growth regulators is Auxin, Gibberellin, and Cytokinin.

Answer: Auxin, Gibberellin, Cytokinin

126462.subject: Botany
126462.text: What is the purpose of elemental analysis?
options: To determine the functional groups in living tissues
To determine the elemental composition of living tissues
To determine the organic and inorganic constituents in living tissues
126462.sol: One weighs a small amount of a living tissue (say a leaf or liver and this is called wet weight) and dry it. All the water, evaporates. The remaining material gives dry weight. Now if the tissue is fully burnt, all the carbon compounds are oxidised to gaseous form (CO2 , water vapour) and are removed. What is remaining is called ‘ash’. This ash contains inorganic elements (like calcium, magnesium etc). Inorganic compounds like sulphate, phosphate, etc., are also seen in the acid-soluble fraction. Therefore elemental analysis gives elemental composition of living tissues in the form of hydrogen, oxygen, chlorine, carbon etc. while analysis for compounds gives an idea of the kind of organic and inorganic constituents present in living tissues.

126709.subject: Botany
126709.text:
Read the following statements regarding the catalytic cycle of enzyme action and the nature of enzyme-substrate interactions:

(A) The formation of the enzyme-substrate (ES) complex is an obligatory but transient phenomenon.
(B) Substrate binding induces the enzyme to alter its shape, forming a highly stable intermediate.
(C) The active site breaks the chemical bonds of the substrate to form the enzyme-product complex.
(D) The transition state structure is formed after the enzyme releases the products.

How many of the above statements are correct?
126709.sol:
Statement (A) is correct. According to NCERT, the formation of the ES complex is an obligatory and transient phenomenon during enzyme catalysis.

Statement (B) is incorrect. While substrate binding does induce the enzyme to alter its shape (induced fit), the intermediate transition state formed is unstable, not highly stable.

Statement (C) is correct. In the catalytic cycle, once the enzyme fits tightly around the substrate, the active site breaks the chemical bonds of the substrate to form the enzyme-product (EP) complex.

Statement (D) is incorrect. The transition state structure is formed while the substrate is bound to the enzyme's active site, long before the enzyme releases the products.

Therefore, exactly two statements ((A) and (C)) are correct.

Answer: Two

127342.subject: Botany
127342.text:
Match List-I (Utilisation Category) with List-II (Examples/Definitions):

List-IList-II
(A) Narrowly Utilitarian(I) Oxygen production and Pollination
(B) Broadly Utilitarian(II) $25,000$ species of plants used for medicine
(C) Ethical Argument(III) Exploring molecular/genetic level diversity for products
(D) Bioprospecting(IV) Philosophically sharing the planet with all species

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
127342.sol:
Refer: NCERT | Class 12 | Page: 223 - 224 | Paragraph: 5,6 - 1,2

Narrowly utilitarian arguments for conserving biodiversity are based on direct economic benefits derived from nature, such as food, firewood, fibre, and medicines. More than $25,000$ species of plants are used in traditional medicines. Thus, (A) matches with (II).

Broadly utilitarian arguments are based on the ecosystem services provided by nature, such as oxygen production and pollination. Thus, (B) matches with (I).

The ethical argument relates to the philosophical and spiritual realization that we share the planet with millions of other species, each having an intrinsic value. Thus, (C) matches with (IV).

Bioprospecting is the exploration of molecular, genetic, and species-level diversity to obtain products of economic importance. Thus, (D) matches with (III).

The correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III).

Answer: (1) (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)

127833.text:
Assertion : Rice field is an ecosystem for plants and animals.
Reason : Gut of human/animals is an ecosystem for flora and fauna.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false
127833.sol:
The human digestive system carries about trillions of microorganisms colonising the gut making an amazing ecosystem that live together in harmony. In this context human intestine is said to be rich in flora and fauna. The microorganisms perform a host of useful functions, such as fermenting unused energy substrates, training the immune system, preventing growth of harmful, pathogenic bacteria, regulating the development of the gut, producing vitamins for the host (such as biotin and vitamin $\mathrm{K}$ ), and producing hormones to direct the host to store fats.
Fish culture is sometimes done in combination with a rice crop, so that fish are grown in the water in the paddy field. Thus, a rice field is an example of ecosystem inhabiting both plants and animals.

128005.subject: Zoology
128005.text: What part of the frog is used as food by man in some countries?
128005.sol: " Frogs have well organised male and female reproductive systems. Male reproductive organs consist of a pair of yellowish ovoid testes , which are found adhered to the upper part of kidneys by a double fold of peritoneum called mesorchium. Vasa efferentia are 10-12 in number that arise from testes. They enter the kidneys on their side and open into Bidder’s canal. Finally it communicates with the urinogenital duct that comes out of the kidneys and opens into the cloaca. The cloaca is a small, median chamber that is used to pass faecal matter, urine and sperms to the exterior. The female reproductive organs include a pair of ovaries The ovaries are situated near kidneys and there is no functional connection with kidneys. A pair of oviduct arising from the ovaries opens into the cloaca separately. A mature female can lay 2500 to 3000 ova at a time. Fertilisation is external and takes place in water. Development involves a larval stage called tadpole. Tadpole undergoes metamorphosis to form the adult.Frogs are beneficial for mankind because they eat insects and protect the crop. Frogs maintain ecological balance because these serve as an important link of food chain and food web in the ecosystem. In some countries the muscular legs of frog are used as food by man.
